subject: Intermittent large-packet drops after private cutover — Brookline Health
body:
From: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@brooklinehealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Upload failures after private cutover (large files)

Tessa,

We cut over our private link to Redwood last night and since then our clinical imaging uploads (large files, ~2–15 MB single requests) are intermittently failing with TCP retries and stalled uploads. The failures are only for larger packets/streams — small traffic (API calls, healthchecks) look fine.

Attached: traceroute_to-redwood.txt and edge-fw-pcap.pcap (PCAP has sample failed upload session).

Quick observations from our side:
- TCP retransmits and repeated zero-window events in the capture.
- I see ICMP Type 3 Code 4 (Fragmentation Needed) coming from 10.240.12.1 (our edge) to 10.0.0.18 (Redwood) in the capture, but clients are still timing out.
- We are running a FastPath edge firewall doing SNAT (outbound-to-internet) and have MSS clamping off by default.

Can you confirm whether anything on your VPC or the transit path might be blocking ICMP fragmentation-needed messages, or whether you see asymmetric return path? This is causing service-impact for one of our uploads flows.

Thanks,
Sam Ortiz
NetOps Lead, Brookline Health
--
Brookline Health

-----
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@brooklinehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 08:34:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Upload failures after private cutover (large files)

Sam — thanks for the quick report and attachments. I’ve looped in our private deployment network leads (Vivek, Grace, Karthik). We’ll triage immediately.

A few immediate asks to help narrow root cause:
- Can you confirm whether your FastPath firewall applies SNAT for egress to the Redwood VPC, or only for internet-bound flows?
- Can you paste the edge firewall outbound NAT rules (the SNAT range and whether there’s any port-preserving setting)?
- Do you have any upstream MTU changes between your on-prem edge and the transit (e.g., MPLS / ethernet MTU reductions)?

I’ll start by checking the VPC SG/NACLs and the transit logs for blocked ICMP.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Technical Account Manager | Redwood Inference

-----
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:00:30 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Upload failures after private cutover (Brookline Health) — triage

Folks — forwarding Brookline’s packet capture and traceroute. Repro steps: their client uploads stall on large payloads only after private cutover. They see ICMP frag-needed from their edge to Redwood but uploads still fail.

Initial theory: either (A) PMTUD blackhole due to ICMP being blocked somewhere between on-prem and the application host, or (B) MTU mismatch plus SNAT rewriters causing path differences (and maybe ephemeral port exhaustion for large concurrent uploads).

Please investigate:
- Vivek, check VPC host-level interfaces and SG logs for dropped ICMP Type 3 code 4 in the last 12 hours.
- Grace, validate our transit/edge transit policies and whether we’re dropping ICMP for the customer’s /29.
- Karthik, review whether our per-host SNAT (egress-proxy) might be rewriting source or path in a way that prevents fragments from reaching the original sender.

I’ll pull their traceroute and the PCAP into the ticket (NET-4821).

Tessa

-----
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 10:20:15 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Upload failures after private cutover (Brookline Health) — first pass analysis

Quick pass on the PCAP and VPC logs:
- I see clear ICMP Type 3 / Code 4 (Fragmentation Needed) packets in their capture: source looks like their edge (10.240.12.1) -> destination our host (10.0.0.18). The payload indicates MTU needed ~1380.
- Our VPC Flow Logs show the SYNs and partial streams arriving at 10.0.0.18. We also see corresponding RSTs from the application host when the client stalls.
- Important: Flow logs/SG logs show an outbound rule set that drops inbound ICMP from the customer CIDR for non-echo types. The SG attached to host 10.0.0.18 currently allows inbound TCP/443 from the customer prefix, but SG stateful behavior is subtle here — the ICMP frag-needed might be classified as unsolicited by the SG because of SNAT translation on our side for some egress path.
- I also see their edge performing SNAT to a small ephemeral range (100.64.0.200-100.64.0.220) in the capture. That range is small for their concurrent upload scale. If the edge runs out of ports it can start reusing 1:1 mappings, producing unexpected flows that our SG may not correlate with existing connection state.

Actionable notes:
1) Recommend Brookline allow ICMP (Type 3) in their firewall egress and allow inbound ICMP on our SG for their CIDR temporarily while we validate.
2) Ask Brookline to enable MSS clamping to 1300 on their FastPath edge — this avoids fragmentation and makes PMTUD unnecessary for path with smaller MTU.
3) Increase their SNAT ephemeral pool or enable port-preserving SNAT to avoid port exhaustion.

I’ll prepare a brief mitigation playbook we can send to them. Also opening NET-4821 with these logs.

Vivek
Senior Network Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

-----
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@brooklinehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, FastPath Firewall Support <support@fastpath-fw.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 11:15:02 -0800
Subject: Re: Upload failures after private cutover (large files) — immediate mitigations and playbook

Sam — thanks for the quick handover. Vivek confirmed we’re seeing ICMP frag-needed in the capture and our SG may be classifying them as unrelated due to SNAT path differences. Two immediate mitigations to try (low risk):

Playbook (for your edge / FastPath team):
- Step 1: Temporarily allow ICMP Type 3 (all codes) from your customer prefix to Redwood (10.0.0.0/24) and on your outbound policy allow replies. This will ensure PMTUD signaling is not blackholed while we test.
- Step 2: Enable MSS clamping on the FastPath edge to 1300 (applies to TCP SYN and outgoing path). This forces endpoints to use smaller segments and avoids fragmented packets.
- Step 3: Expand the SNAT ephemeral port pool to at least 1000 ports per external IP (we recommend 100.64.0.200-100.64.4.250) or enable port-preserving SNAT so your source ports are not rewritten unpredictably.
- Step 4: Collect another PCAP (client->edge->host) after changes and share; attach to NET-4821.

Attached: playbook-mss-clamp.txt and packet-capture-analysis.txt (highlights of Vivek’s observables).

FastPath team — if you have a recommended command snippet to apply MSS clamp and show current SNAT pool size, please paste it here and we’ll coordinate the change window.

Sam — if you want we can do the SG change on our side temporarily to accept ICMP from your prefix; let us know if you prefer to make the inbound changes on your FW first.

Regards,
Tessa Morgan
Technical Account Manager | Redwood Inference

-----
From: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@brooklinehealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, FastPath Firewall Support <support@fastpath-fw.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 16:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Upload failures after private cutover (large files) — resolved

Tessa/Vivek/Grace/Karthik — quick update: applied MSS clamp 1300 and increased SNAT pool on FastPath per playbook. Also temporarily allowed ICMP Type 3 between our edges and Redwood host.

Result: uploads are stable for several hours under the same load; no retransmit storms observed in new captures. We’ve attached a short capture and confirm the fragmentation-needed messages now result in smaller MSS or are avoided entirely.

Thanks for the quick triage and the clear playbook. Please leave NET-4821 open for one week while we monitor, but we consider the issue mitigated.

Sam Ortiz
NetOps Lead, Brookline Health
--
Brookline Health
